title: [Chapitre] V. Algèbre des figures : notes manuscrites (14/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 15-17): Grothendieck is building an 'algebra of figures' 𝔉(𝓛) over a point-set 𝓛. Figures carry an order ≤ (sub-figure), a disjointness relation and supports |F| ⊂ 𝓛. Page 15 shows that disjointness is set-theoretic disjointness of supports, so complementation is set complement, and that 𝔉(L') for L' ⊂ L sits inside 𝔉(L) as a saturated subset.

Page 16 does four things.

(1) Reconstruction from order data. The set 𝔉(𝓛) can be recovered from the poset 𝓛_≤, or from (𝒰_≤, compatibility). The order on 𝔉 is recovered from the order on supports, and likewise complementation.

(2) The NB. It is partly illegible. It seems to describe 𝔉 as made of closed parts, or limits, whose interiors satisfy some compatibility.

(3) Stone space. Recovering things purely from the order and Boolean structure of supports does not give 𝓛 itself. It gives the Stone space 𝓛̂ of the Boolean algebra of supports. Since supports are arbitrary subsets of 𝓛, this algebra is P(𝓛) and 𝓛̂ = β𝓛, the Stone–Čech compactification of discrete 𝓛. 𝓛 is recovered as the set of isolated points of 𝓛̂. This suggests redoing the theory over an arbitrary compact totally disconnected (Stone) space X, with 𝔉 = admissible families of clopen subsets of X.

(4) Finite versus infinite. With finite figures and families, supports are exactly the clopens of X. With infinite figures or families, the clopens are no longer closed under the needed infinite operations. Support/cosupport pairs must then be replaced by pairs (U,V) of opens with:
- U = int(∁V) = ext V and V = int(∁U) = ext U;
- Ū ∩ V̄ = X ∖ (U ∪ V), a common boundary.
These are exactly the regular open sets U = int(Ū). This is the standard passage from the Boolean algebra of clopens of the Stone space of B to its completion RO(X), the Dedekind–MacNeille completion of B.

The page thus moves from a set-based theory of figures to a Stone-duality / regular-open-algebra framework.
errors: Minor redundancy: when the support algebra is P(𝓛), the Stone space β𝓛 is extremally disconnected. Its regular opens are then exactly its clopens, so the infinite-family modification changes nothing in that case. It matters only for general Stone spaces X, which is presumably Grothendieck's intended generalization.
The NB and the marginal note are too illegible to verify; no mathematical error is detectable in what can be read.

ideas.what: Recovering the base set as isolated points of the Stone space of the Boolean algebra of supports
ideas.modern_name: Stone duality; β of a discrete set; atoms of P(L) correspond to isolated points

ideas.what: Redoing the theory of figures over a compact totally disconnected space, with figures as families of clopens
ideas.modern_name: Boolean-algebra / Stone-space formulation of region-based (point-free) geometry

ideas.what: Support/cosupport pairs (U,V) with U = ext V, V = ext U, meeting along a common boundary; equivalently regular open sets
ideas.modern_name: Regular open algebra RO(X); completion of a Boolean algebra
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tarski, MacNeille, Stone (1930s); Tarski's geometry of solids (1929) uses regular opens as regions

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 'algèbre des figures' converges on regular open sets as the right support/cosupport objects for infinite figures. This is exactly the framework of Tarski's geometry of solids and of later mereotopology and contact algebras (de Vries, Düntsch–Vakarelov). Grothendieck's notes do not cite that tradition, and that tradition does not know of these notes. His added structure (multiplicities, figures as 'multistables', i-connectedness of interiors on p.17) could be compared with contact-algebra axiomatics.
missed.quote: les couples supports-cosupports de X, par les couples (U,V) d'ouverts de X ... i.e. les ouverts U tels que U = int(Ū)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a modest historical link: Grothendieck's late foundational 'tame' geometry program meets region-based or mereotopological theories of space. It is only of interest to someone studying his 1986 'figures' program.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on the page is standard: Stone duality, β of a discrete set, regular open algebras. The only mildly interesting point is that Grothendieck's figure-theory independently arrives at the regular-open/mereotopological framework.
transcription_corrections: 'le complété de Stone' is more likely 'le compactifié de Stone' (𝓛̂ is a compactification).
'X̄̄' doubled bars should be single closures: Ū ∩ V̄ = X ∖ (U ∪ V).
'refaire la théorie en termes d'un espace compact [tot.] discontinu X': read as totally disconnected compact space.
's'identifient aux parties o. o. f. de X' means 'parties à la fois ouvertes et fermées' (clopens).
Read 'Mais si on prend des figures infinies ou des familles infinies, on change ...' ('on' and 'ou' are confused in the machine text).
'par les couples (U,V) d'ouverts de X identifiés aux Ū' is uncertain; the sense is identification of pairs (U,V) with the regular opens U.
